title: Job Chapter 34 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Job chapter 34 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Job Chapter 34 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Job Chapter 34.

questions.question: Who answered and spoke in Job 34?
questions.explanation: Elihu is the one who answered and spoke in Job 34, as stated in Job 34:1.

questions.question: What should wise men do according to Job 34:2?
questions.explanation: Job 34:2 instructs wise men to listen to Elihu's words.

questions.question: In Job 34:3, what is compared to tasting meat?
questions.explanation: Job 34:3 states, 'For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat.'

questions.question: According to Job 34:4, what should they choose?
questions.explanation: Job 34:4 encourages them to choose judgment and know what is good.

questions.question: True or False: Job claims he is righteous and that God has taken away his judgment.
questions.explanation: Job 34:5 confirms that Job claims he is righteous and feels God has taken away his judgment.

questions.question: What does Job say about his wound in Job 34:6?
options: It is a result of sin
questions.explanation: Job 34:6 states, 'my wound is incurable without transgression.'

questions.question: True or False: Job is compared to a man who drinks up scorning like water.
questions.explanation: Job 34:7 compares Job to a man who drinks up scorning like water.

questions.question: According to Job 34:9, what does Job claim profits a man nothing?
questions.explanation: Job 34:9 states that Job claims it profits a man nothing to delight himself with God.

questions.question: True or False: Job 34:10 states that it is far from God to do wickedness.
questions.explanation: Job 34:10 confirms that it is far from God to do wickedness.

questions.question: What does Job 34:11 say that God will render to a man?
questions.explanation: Job 34:11 indicates that God will render to a man according to his work.

questions.question: True or False: Job 34:12 states that God will do wickedly.
questions.explanation: Job 34:12 clearly states that God will not do wickedly.

questions.question: In Job 34:13, who has given God charge over the earth?
questions.explanation: Job 34:13 poses the question, 'Who hath given him a charge over the earth?' indicating no one has done so.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of Job 34:14 regarding man?
questions.explanation: Job 34:14 suggests that if God sets His heart upon man, it relates to man's accountability.

questions.question: In Job 34, what comes FIRST in Elihu's instructions?
options: Do not lie against your right
questions.explanation: Job 34:2 comes first where Elihu instructs the wise men to hear his words.

medium.title: Job Chapter 34 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Job Chapter 34 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Job 34:15 say will happen to all flesh?
questions.explanation: Job 34:15 states, 'All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust,' indicating the mortality of all living beings.

questions.question: According to Job 34:20, what will happen to the mighty?
options: They shall be taken away without hand
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be taken away without hand
questions.explanation: Job 34:20 mentions that 'the mighty shall be taken away without hand,' illustrating God's sovereign power in judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Job 34:12 states that God will do wickedly.
questions.explanation: Job 34:12 asserts, 'Yea, surely God will not do wickedly,' affirming God's inherent justice.

questions.question: How does Job 34:19 describe God's view of the rich and the poor?
options: He regards the rich more than the poor
He accepts not the persons of princes
questions.correctAnswer: He accepts not the persons of princes
questions.explanation: Job 34:19 emphasizes that God does not show favoritism towards the rich, as 'he accepteth not the persons of princes.'

questions.question: What does Job 34:21 indicate about God's awareness of man?
options: He observes the ways of man
He is blind to human behavior
questions.correctAnswer: He observes the ways of man
questions.explanation: Job 34:21 states, 'For his eyes are upon the ways of man,' highlighting God's omniscience regarding human actions.

questions.question: If a person turns back from God's ways, what does Job 34:27 say they cause?
options: They cause the cry of the poor to come unto God
questions.correctAnswer: They cause the cry of the poor to come unto God
questions.explanation: Job 34:28 indicates that turning away from God leads to the cry of the poor being heard by Him, emphasizing the consequences of rebellion.

questions.question: True or False: Job is described in Job 34:35 as speaking with wisdom.
questions.explanation: Job 34:35 states, 'Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom,' indicating his lack of understanding.

questions.question: What does Job 34:23 say about God's judgment upon man?
options: He will lay upon man more than right
He will not lay upon man more than right
questions.correctAnswer: He will not lay upon man more than right
questions.explanation: Job 34:23 asserts, 'For he will not lay upon man more than right,' emphasizing God's fairness in judgment.

questions.question: According to Job 34:26, how does God treat wicked men?
options: He strikes them as wicked men in the open sight of others
questions.correctAnswer: He strikes them as wicked men in the open sight of others
questions.explanation: Job 34:26 states that God 'striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others,' indicating public judgment of evil.

questions.question: What does Job 34:32 request from God regarding unseen iniquity?
options: That it be revealed and taught
questions.correctAnswer: That it be revealed and taught
questions.explanation: Job 34:32 expresses a desire for God to 'teach thou me' about unseen iniquity, showing a heart for understanding and repentance.

questions.question: In what way does Job 34:18 challenge the notion of condemning authority figures?
options: It suggests they are always just
It asks if it is fit to say to a king, 'Thou art wicked?'
questions.correctAnswer: It asks if it is fit to say to a king, 'Thou art wicked?'
questions.explanation: Job 34:18 poses the question of whether it is appropriate to call a king wicked, prompting reflection on justice and authority.

questions.question: True or False: Job 34:36 expresses a desire for Job to be tried for his answers against wicked men.
questions.explanation: Job 34:36 states, 'My desire is that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men,' indicating a call for thorough examination.

questions.question: What does Job 34:4 encourage people to do regarding judgment?
options: To choose judgment and know what is good
questions.correctAnswer: To choose judgment and know what is good
questions.explanation: Job 34:4 encourages individuals to 'choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what is good,' promoting discernment in moral choices.

hard.title: Job Chapter 34 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Job Chapter 34.

questions.question: What does Elihu urge wise men to do in Job 34?
questions.explanation: Elihu asks the wise men to hear his words and give ear to him, indicating the importance of listening to his counsel (Job 34:2).

questions.question: According to Job 34, what does God not do?
options: He does not listen to prayers
questions.explanation: Elihu emphasizes that it is far from God to do wickedness and the Almighty to commit iniquity (Job 34:10).

questions.question: In Job 34, what happens to the mighty according to Elihu?
questions.explanation: Elihu states that in a moment the mighty shall die and be troubled at midnight (Job 34:20).

questions.question: What does Elihu say about God's judgment in Job 34?
questions.explanation: Elihu asserts that God will not lay upon man more than is right, ensuring fairness in His judgment (Job 34:23).

questions.question: In Job 34, what does Elihu say happens when God hides His face?
questions.explanation: Elihu states that when God hides His face, no one can behold Him, whether it is against a nation or a man (Job 34:29).

questions.question: How does Elihu describe the actions of the hypocrite in Job 34?
questions.explanation: Elihu warns that the hypocrite should not reign, lest the people be ensnared (Job 34:30).

questions.question: What does Job claim about his own state, according to Elihu in Job 34?
questions.explanation: Elihu references Job's assertion that he is righteous and that God has taken away his judgment (Job 34:5).

questions.question: According to Job 34:35, how does Elihu describe Job's words?
questions.explanation: Elihu claims that Job has spoken without knowledge and that his words were without wisdom (Job 34:35).

questions.question: Which Psalm echoes the theme of God hearing the cry of the afflicted, similar to Job 34:28?
questions.explanation: Psalm 34:17 states that the Lord hears the cries of the righteous, paralleling Elihu's assertion that God hears the cry of the afflicted (Job 34:28).

questions.question: In Job 34:31, what does Elihu suggest should be said to God regarding chastisement?
questions.explanation: Elihu suggests it is right to say to God, 'I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more' (Job 34:31).

questions.question: True or False: Elihu believes that God will punish man for more than he deserves.
questions.explanation: Elihu clearly states that God will not lay upon man more than is right (Job 34:23), indicating that God is fair in His judgments.

questions.question: True or False: Elihu advocates for a trial of Job to test his responses.
questions.explanation: Elihu expresses a desire that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men (Job 34:36).

questions.question: What literary device is prominently featured in Elihu's speech in Job 34?
questions.explanation: Elihu's speech contains chiastic structures, particularly in the way he presents contrasting ideas about God's justice and human actions, which is common in biblical poetry.

questions.question: What Hebrew word meaning 'to turn back' is used in Job 34:27 to describe those who do not consider God's ways?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Shub' means to turn back or return, and is used in Job 34:27 to describe those who turned back from God and did not consider His ways.

theological.title: Job Chapter 34 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Job Chapter 34 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Elihu urge wise men to do at the beginning of his speech?
questions.explanation: Elihu begins by calling upon wise men to hear his words and give ear to him, which is stated in Job 34:2.

questions.question: According to Job 34:10, what is far from God?
questions.explanation: Elihu asserts that it is far from God to do wickedness, as he clearly states in Job 34:10.

questions.question: What does Elihu claim will happen to a man according to his ways?
questions.explanation: Elihu states that God will render to a man according to his ways, emphasizing the principle of divine judgment in Job 34:11.

questions.question: What does Job claim about his relationship with God?
questions.explanation: Elihu mentions that Job claims to be righteous and feels that God has taken away his judgment in Job 34:5.

questions.question: What does Job feel about his suffering, according to Elihu?
options: It is a test of faith
It is an opportunity for growth
questions.explanation: Job expresses that he feels wronged by God, claiming he is righteous in Job 34:5, indicating a sense of injustice in his suffering.

questions.question: What does Elihu say about God's governance over the earth?
options: He has given charge to man
questions.explanation: Elihu questions who has given God a charge over the earth, implying His sovereign authority in Job 34:13.

questions.question: What is revealed about God’s justice in Job 34:12?
questions.explanation: Elihu affirms that God will not do wickedly, asserting His commitment to justice in Job 34:12.

questions.question: According to Job 34:29, what can occur when God hides His face?
questions.explanation: Elihu notes that when God hides His face, trouble may ensue, which is mentioned in Job 34:29.

questions.question: What does Elihu say about the hypocrite in Job 34:30?
questions.explanation: Elihu warns that the hypocrite should not reign, which could ensnare the people, as stated in Job 34:30.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 31-32 convey about repentance?
questions.explanation: Elihu emphasizes the need for acknowledgment of wrongdoing and a desire to learn from God in Job 34:31-32.

questions.question: How does Elihu characterize Job's statements in Job 34:35?
questions.explanation: Elihu critiques Job's words, stating they were spoken without knowledge, as noted in Job 34:35.

questions.question: What is the essence of Elihu's desire regarding Job in Job 34:36?
options: To try him unto the end
questions.correctAnswer: To try him unto the end
questions.explanation: Elihu desires that Job be tried until the end, reflecting his concern over Job's responses to God in Job 34:36.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that God is unjust in His treatment of humanity. What does Job 34:10-12 actually teach?
questions.explanation: Elihu asserts that it is far from God to commit wickedness and that He will not pervert judgment, demonstrating God's inherent justice in Job 34:10-12.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Job 34:21 regarding His oversight of humanity?
questions.explanation: Elihu emphasizes that God's eyes are upon the ways of man, indicating His all-knowing nature in Job 34:21.

questions.question: What does Job 34:7 suggest about Job's attitude towards scorn?
options: He drinks it up like water
questions.correctAnswer: He drinks it up like water
questions.explanation: Elihu expresses that Job drinks up scorn like water, indicating Job's familiarity and acceptance of criticism in Job 34:7.
